date_note: ZDNet Korea (23 Nov) says the Fair Trade Commission announced the result on the 23rd; the page gives no earlier day.
title: South Korea's Fair Trade Commission asks for correction of 73 unfair bank terms, including blanket liability clauses
impact: Correction requested from the Financial Services Commission; not a binding order on the banks.
summary: South Korea's Fair Trade Commission said on 23 November it reviewed 1550 bank and mutual savings bank terms made or revised in 2025 and found 73 unfair clauses, asking the Financial Services Commission to correct them, ZDNet Korea reports. According to the report, 9 banks and 1 savings bank had blanket clauses making customers responsible for all results of account or password misuse and excluding the bank's liability for losses including data loss.
plain: Korea's competition regulator found 73 unfair clauses in bank terms and asked the financial regulator to have them fixed. Some clauses make customers responsible for all results of account or password misuse.
exec: Korean banks may have to drop blanket clauses that put all account-misuse results on customers and excluded the bank's liability for losses such as data loss, per ZDNet Korea.

evidence.quote: 공정위는 23일 2025년 제·개정된 은행 및 상호저축은행 약관 1550개를 심사한 결과, 금융소비자 권익을 침해하는 불공정 약관 조항 73개(17개 유형)를 적발해 금융위원회에 시정을 요청했다고 밝혔다.

validation.note: One publisher read: ZDNet Korea (23 Nov), which states the 23 November announcement, 1550 terms reviewed, 73 unfair clauses (17 types) and the request to the Financial Services Commission. The FTC's own press release was not found or read; the article names no banks.

review.note: stronger than the source: title and plain said all 73 clauses were hacking liability; the article body never mentions hacking; reworded title, plain, exec. Date, 1550 and 73 figures and the evidence quote match ZDNet Korea.
